raw_response:
I have been farming this land for 40 years, so I know what to do. Let me think it through piece by piece.

My 10.9 mu — I will keep 3 mu for cotton on the sandier plot near the road (that ground never did well for wheat anyway), and the other 7.9 mu I will run wheat-maize like always. That is how my neighbors around me do it too.

**Wheat (7.9 mu, winter):** I plant in October after the maize comes off. I use improved variety seed — Jimai or whatever the dealer at the county town has in stock this year, usually around 15 kg/mu of seed. For base fertilizer I put down one bag of compound fertilizer (15-15-15, that is 50 jin, so about 25 kg per mu), plus I top-dress with urea at jointing — maybe 15 kg urea per mu. That gives me around 18 kg N, 8 kg P, 8 kg K. Last year my wheat gave me about 480 kg/mu, so I aim for that again. I irrigate three times — before winter, at jointing, and at grain filling. Well water is cheap but the electricity adds up. Spray herbicide once, then one spray for aphids and powdery mildew together. Plough before planting.

**Maize (7.9 mu, summer):** Right after wheat harvest in June I plant hybrid maize — Zhengdan or Xianyu, whatever seed the neighbors had good luck with. No ploughing, just direct seed into the wheat stubble with the seeder, that saves time and money. One bag compound fertilizer at planting, then 20 kg urea at the big trumpet stage. About 22 kg N total. Irrigate twice if the rain is not enough. Spray once for borer. I expect 580 kg/mu — last year was 600, the year before 550.

**Cotton (3 mu, spring):** Cotton is more work but the price has been okay. I plant in late April, improved variety seed, maybe Jinmian. Plough the land first. Base fertilizer one bag compound plus some extra potash because cotton likes potassium — 15 kg N, 8 kg P, 12 kg K. Top dress urea at flowering, 10 kg more. Irrigate 3-4 times. Cotton needs spraying many times — bollworm, aphid, spider mite — I will spray maybe 6-7 times through the season. Expect 240 kg/mu of seed cotton.

My wife helps with cotton picking, and I hire two people for a few days at peak. My son sends money so I am not too tight, but I still do not waste fertilizer.
